overview: Infinite bliss, known as 'Ananta Sukha' in Jain philosophy, refers to the ultimate state of happiness and peace experienced by a liberated soul (Siddha). This state is achieved when the soul is freed from all karmic bonds, which are considered the root cause of suffering and ignorance. Infinite bliss is characterized by eternal joy and absence of pain, resulting from the complete realization of the soul's true nature. In Jainism, this state is attainable through rigorous practice of right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct, collectively known as the three jewels or 'Ratnatraya'. The concept underscores the Jain belief in the potential for every soul to achieve liberation through its efforts.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umasvati
primary_sources.translation: Infinite perception, knowledge, bliss, and energy are the characteristics of a liberated soul.
primary_sources.notes: This text is a key scripture in Jain philosophy, outlining the attributes of a Siddha.

misconceptions.myth: Infinite bliss can be experienced in the material world.
misconceptions.reality: According to Jainism, infinite bliss is only attainable after the soul achieves liberation and is free from all karmic bonds.
